What is obesity

Obesity is a medical condition in which excess amount of body fat is accumulated i.e., more than 20% of an individual’s ideal body fat. Overweight is different from obesity. Obesity may have severe effects on health leading to reduced life expectancy. It increases the likelihood of various diseases such as Diabetes, Heart disease, Osteoarthritis, certain types cancer etc. it might have adverse effect on both physical and mental conditions. Obesity is caused due to the excess amount of food energy intake, lack of physical activity and genetic susceptibility. Insufficient sleep, increased use of medications (that can cause weight gain), pregnancy at a later age, epigenetic risk factors passed on generations etc contribute to obesity. It is very important to treat obesity as it leads to many chronic illnesses. BMI (Body Mass Index) is used to identify an obese person. It is calculated using a person’s height and weight. BMI equals a persons weight in kilograms and is divided by their in meters squared.
